produced values at is recomputed under the new one.

parameter_id.description:
The catalog parameter read into the variable. NULL on a site source, which names a column
of the site's own row instead; a row carries exactly one of the two (DB CHECK).

site_property.description:
The column of `sites` read into the variable, for a property of the station rather than a
measurement taken at the visit. NULL on a parameter source.

alignment.description:
How the binder reaches a reading for this variable (Q230): `exact` at the instant being
computed, `hold` for the last value measured at or before it, which is what a
visit-measured input read by a calculation on a stream needs. DB CHECK over the two.

parameter_id.description:
The catalog parameter read into the variable. NULL on a site source, which names a column
of the site's own row instead; a row carries exactly one of the two (DB CHECK).

site_property.description:
The column of `sites` read into the variable, for a property of the station rather than a
measurement taken at the visit. NULL on a parameter source.

DerivedSeries.description:
What one formula of the set produced over the window. A step carries `intermediate`, so a
reader can tell the value the set publishes from the working number that fed it.

DraftFormula.description:
One formula of a draft set, as the calculation editor holds it: the same fields the stored
formula carries, without an id, because the point is to run what is not saved yet.

call.description: The R call that raised, when the runner named one.

DraftRunFailureKind.description:
Which of the three things that end a draft run happened, so a caller can render the failure
where it belongs (the body form, the script pane, or the runner's own state) instead of
reading the message.

constants.description:
Constant values in place of the catalog. As in a stored test case, an override must name
every constant the manifest declares; omit the field to read the catalog.

inputs.description:
The calculate request body this draft is run with: the manifest's params, plus its curve
slots given either as a `standard_curve_id` or as literal coefficients.

oneOf.description:
Why the run ended without results. A failure here is a finding about the draft, not a
failed request, so it travels at 200 next to `lint`.

lint.description:
What the save path would say about this script. Findings neither stop a draft from running
nor depend on it running: the runner container is the boundary either way, and an author
mid-edit wants everything that is wrong in one answer. `POST /tool_scripts/{id}/versions`
still refuses to store them. A constant the table does not hold is reported here and left
out of the values the script receives.

ran.description: True when `results` and the rest of the run fields are present; false when `failure` is.

tool_version.description:
Carries the runner the request reached; the version fields are null, nothing here is
stored.

DraftRunResults.description: What the script produced, present only when the run reached the end.

constants.description: The constant values the server resolved and passed to the runner, by name.

DynamicFlag.description:
A detection the parse tree cannot complete: `any` is what a caller branches on, the
expressions are what it shows when it does.

EditDecision.description: The decision an edit request carries: what to do, and the one value it needs.

target_id.description: The curve, calibration or instrument the decision names.

EditOption.description: What may be done to one row, given what produced it.

preview_id.description: Required on a commit: the id the preview returned. A commit of anything else is refused.

rows_decided.description: The decisions this edit recorded, which is what a rollback names.

set_id.description: The set the decisions were recorded under, rolled back as one act.

paused.description:
Operator-desired pause state, persisted server-side; honored before the
initial sync so a restart cannot undo a pause.

sync_interval_secs.description:
Operator-set scheduled sync cadence, persisted server-side. None leaves the
service on its own `SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS`.

site_id.description: Audit every event at this site. Omit both fields to audit every site.

finding.description: The oldest open finding for this cell, slot-keyed or placed through its stream's pairing.

has_provenance.description: A server-built tool-run blob is stored on the measurement.

origin.description:
How these readings reached the store: `manual`, `csv`, `api` or `sync`. A measurement
without a tool-run blob is not therefore hand-entered; it may be an import or a batch, and
the two are different answers to "did a person type this".

provenance_kind.description:
Where the value came from, as the row records it: `tool_run` | `chain` | `csv_import` |
`manual` | `batch` | `sync` | `derived`. Narrower than `origin`, which reads
the stream alone and cannot tell a hand entry from a tool save on the same channel.

read_by.description:
The calculations that read this parameter, by tool name. A person typing into a field needs
to see which script it feeds while typing it, not after the save.

record.description:
The instant's assembled record for this stream, the same shape `/readings/provenance`
serves, so the point record opened from the grid needs no second fetch.

served_value.description: The value serving arm reports: sample mean, else the lowest unflagged live replicate.

source_system.description:
Which feed these replicates came in on. Two streams can serve one slot at one instant, and
then the grid shows two rows under one parameter name with nothing distinguishing them.

tool.description: The blob's tool name, when one exists.

tool_run_id.description:
The run behind the value, when a tool computed it. The trace endpoint replays it, which is
what lets a cell show the formula rather than only the name of what ran.

written_by.description:
The calculation that writes this parameter, when one does. Its value is a computed output,
not a measurement, and editing it is a different act from editing an input.

unverified.description:
The field day is pending a manager's ruling (Q177). Its measurements cannot be verified
until it is.

withdrawn_at.description: When the visit was rejected, its readings withdrawn beside it.

EventPreview.description:
What the calculation chain would produce at a visit, given what the operator has typed and not
saved. Nothing in it is stored and nothing in it names a run: Save executes the same walk and
mints the run the stored values cite (Q212).

calculations.description:
One entry per calculation that ran, in the order it ran, with the inputs, constants,
curves and versions it consumed.

not_applicable.description: Calculations the site declares nothing for.

skipped.description: Calculations that did not run at this visit, as `(tool, reason)`.

unchanged.description:
Calculations whose stored run already consumed exactly this: the slot keeps the value it
holds.

calculation.description:
Hold the findings to the ones one calculation raised. A narrowing, so it needs a scope
beside it.

constant.description: Only visits whose stored provenance names this constant. A scope in its own right.

end.description: Visits collected at or before this instant.

only_findings.description: Only visits with an open missing- or stale-output finding.

site_id.description: Recompute every visit at this site.

start.description: Visits collected at or after this instant.

version.description:
Every visit a script version produced values at, as the stored provenance names it. A
scope of its own: this is what an author's migrate arm asks for.

ExistingParamRef.description:
A catalog parameter a plan entry collides with, and what already depends on it. "Exists" on its
own does not say where or whether anything uses it, which is the question an operator has to
answer to resolve a units conflict.

ExpectedGroup.description: The replicate indexes a client read for one group before it built its save.

decimal_places.description: `site_parameters.decimal_places` for the slot, null when it declares none.

read_by.description:
The calculations that read this parameter, by tool name, so every cell of the column says
what a typed value feeds whichever visit it is typed at.

units.description:
The unit the column's numbers are in, from the site's slot when it declares one and the
catalog default otherwise. A grid of bare numbers cannot be read without it.

written_by.description:
The calculation that writes this parameter, when one does. The column's values are computed
outputs, so the grid reads them and sends a correction back through the calculation (Q8)
rather than offering a keystroke.

ExternalSource.description:
How a parameter the site does not measure itself is attributed wherever it is read. The
MeteoSwiss terms ask for the attribution on anything published from the feed, so the line is
built here rather than composed by each reader.

station.description: The station the values are read from.

system.description: The feed, as its rows are keyed (`meteoswiss`).

FieldFormula.description: A field whose value is the difference of two other fields of the same row.

subtract.description: `[minuend, subtrahend]`, both naming fields of the same structure.

dry_run.description: Report the count the write would return and change nothing.

calculations.description:
Under `dry_run`, the calculations the flagged parameter feeds and the outputs each would
rewrite. Flagging changes the served value, so it changes what a calculation reads; the
consequence is reported before the write, not discovered after it.

ForeignCurveUse.description: Readings corrected by a curve their own instrument does not own, grouped by the pair.

standard_curve_id.description: The curve they are corrected by, which belongs to `curve_sensor_id`.

FormulaDraftRunRequest.description:
Run a formula calculation's unsaved formula set at a visit. The formulas replace the stored
set for this run only; nothing is written.

constants.description: Constant values in place of the catalog; omit to read the catalog.

inputs.description:
The calculate request body: `site_id`, `collected_at`, replicate lists and any value
overriding what the visit holds.

manifest.description:
The manifest the formula set implies: its params, outputs, constants, curve slots and the
site and event inputs, in the shape `GET /tools` serves.

ran.description: True when the run fields are present; false when `failure` is.

FormulaDraftRunResults.description: What the formula set produced, present only when the run reached the end.

event_inputs.description: The visit's stored values the run read, as `{param, parameter_code, parameter_id, value}`.

site_inputs.description: The site properties the run read, as `{property, param, value}`.

skipped.description: Outputs the run did not produce, each with its reason.

trace.description: Each formula as it was evaluated, with the values it read per cell.

GivenUpOutput.description: A catalog parameter a formula published until this save ticked it as a step.

code.description: The formula's code, which is the catalog row's code too.

read_by.description:
The formulas that read the parameter, by code: each of them now reads a value nothing
refreshes.

readings_retained.description:
Readings stored under the parameter. They stay, and ticking the formula back as an output
publishes them again.

sites.description: The sites holding a slot of the parameter, by name.

oneOf.description: The instrument's windowed calibration covering `time`, applied first.

composed_equation.description: Both curves folded into one line, present when both apply.

oneOf.description: The operator's hand-picked curve, applied to the base's output.

input.description:
The named input of the referenced tool run this reading stores: the measured value the run
consumed at `replicate_index`, stored raw. A curve the run applied is not a correction of
this row, so `standard_curve_id` is admitted here and the database applies it (ADR 0003).
A `replicates` input stores one reading per position; a numeric input the manifest binds to
a visit parameter (`event_inputs`) stores one at replicate 0, correcting what the visit
holds. A numeric input the manifest binds to nothing is a run-only setting and is refused.

output.description:
The named output of the referenced tool run this reading stores. With `tool_run_id` every
reading names either an `output` or an `input`, and is refused otherwise; the reading's
`value` must be the run's value for that output.

standard_curve_id.description:
The standard curve the operator fitted for this measurement, typically per microplate. It is
applied on top of the instrument's base calibration, which the server resolves from the
sensor's windows at `time`. The stored row carries the measured `raw_value`, both curve
references and the value they produce together, so a recorded identity base and an
unrecorded one stay distinguishable.

check_id.description:
A `seasonal_checks` row (from `/readings/seasonal_check`) covering this save's values.
When present, every reading's (parameter, value) must have been screened by that check —
the portal's "any edit resets Check", enforced server-side. The check itself is advisory;
naming a check that does not cover the values is refused.

dry_run.description: Compute the preview and report existing groups without writing anything.

expected_replicates.description:
What the client believes each group it replaces already holds. A replace retracts the
stored replicates it does not carry, so a save built from a stale read would retract a
repeat somebody else added in the meantime. Naming the indexes refuses that with a 409
describing what is there instead; omitting the field writes without the check.

label.description: Stamped onto the samples rows this request creates or reuses.

oneOf.description:
`replace` atomically rewrites every replicate group this request names. Without it, a
group that is already stored refuses the write with a 409 describing what is there.

tool_run_id.description:
The `tool_runs` row these readings came from (returned by `/tools/{name}/calculate` as
`run_id`). The server builds the provenance blob from that row, so the blob's inputs,
constants, curves and outputs are what the engine resolved, its actor is the calculating
user, and a save cannot claim a run it did not make: every reading must name one of the
run's outputs and carry that output's value.

calculations.description:
The calculations the saved parameters feed and the output parameters each rewrites at the
visit, in run order. Reported on `dry_run` too, so the consequence is known before the
write; the save enqueues the visit's recompute when this is not empty.

created_sample_ids.description:
The samples this request created, as opposed to reused. A caller that wants to act on
exactly the rows it just wrote (the bot flags field submissions for review) can key on these
rather than re-selecting by slot and time, which would also catch a concurrent write.

existing_groups.description:
Replicate groups already stored at the requested (parameter, time) keys, as found before
this request wrote anything.

kept_curated.description:
Curated rows on the grab stream that `mode: replace` left in place: flagged, withdrawn, or
carrying a standard curve the request did not supply. Each group with one raises a
`source_modified` hold, and the value entered at that replicate index is not written.

`serde(default)` reads a response body recorded before the field existed; every save
answers with it, which is what `schema(required)` says.

preview.description:
What each reading stores: the measured value, the curves that apply and the value they
produce together, computed by the code the write itself uses.

replaced.description:
Rows `mode: replace` rewrote in place. Only the grab stream's own rows at the instant are
candidates; rows another source wrote at the same slot and time are untouched.

withdrawn.description:
Replicates stored at the instant that `mode: replace` withdrew because the save no longer
carries them: a cleared cell, or a pasted block narrower than what is there. The value
stays readable and the stamp is reversible; nothing deletes.

GroupAudit.description:
Portal-precomputed mean/sd for one replicate group, sent alongside the
group's readings so the API can compare server-side.

expected_n.description:
Count of non-null replicate cells the portal row carries for this
instant; the API re-counts after admission, so a divergence surfaces
as an n-mismatch hold.

GroupCalculation.description: One calculation of a group's columns, as the group page lists it.

calculations.description:
The calculations that read or publish one of the members, by name. A calculation belongs to
no group (Q169), so the tie between the two is the parameters they share.

sections.description:
The section labels, in the order their first column appears. Empty where no calculation
naming one of these columns declares a section.

sync_interval_secs.description:
Operator-set scheduled sync cadence, persisted server-side. A change here is
adopted by the running service on the next heartbeat.

HoldComputed.description: What river-data computes over the values it stores, which is what it serves.

HoldExpected.description: The source's own statistics for the group, as the hold recorded them.

n.description: The replicate count the source declares, where it declares one.

meets_after.description: Whether the proposed statistics meet it under the audit tolerances.

meets_now.description: Whether the current statistics meet the expectation (they do not, or there is no hold).

tool.description: The calculation a chain finding is against, so its chip opens that calculation.

classification.description:
Signature of the disagreement: `n_mismatch` | `source_sd_matches_n_divisor` |
`stale_subset` | `unexplained`. Computed from the stored expectation and recompute, never
persisted.

relative_delta.description:
Disagreement size relative to the measurement scale: the greater of
`mean_relative_delta` and `sd_relative_delta`; see [`RELATIVE_DELTA_SQL`].

resolution.description: The decision record: latest action plus prior actions under `history`.

sd_relative_delta.description: `|Δsd|` over the same mean-magnitude denominator as `mean_relative_delta`.

site_id.description:
Site and parameter of the paired slot (or of the event finding itself); NULL while the
stream is unpaired.

site_parameter_id.description: The slot the hold is about, which a point record is opened on.

source_name.description: The stream's human name as registered by the source.

stream_id.description: NULL on event-audit findings, which are keyed on (site, parameter, instant) instead.

tool.description: The tool an event finding names.

HoldValue.description:
One stored value with the replicate index it sits at, which is the source's column position and
the only handle a flag can name. A hold recorded before the index travelled with the value
carries the bare number, and no position in that array stands for an index.

ImportCheck.description:
The seasonal Check gate's CSV arm: every cell the file will store as a spot reading, screened
against the site's seasonal distribution for its own month.

check_id.description:
The stored check a commit must name. Set by `dry_run`; echoed by a commit that named one;
`null` on a commit that needed none (nothing outside the range).

findings.description: The cells that warn, in file order, capped at `IMPORT_CHECK_FINDINGS_CAP`.

warnings.description: Cells outside the recorded seasonal range.

ImportChunkRequest.description:
One slice of a file too large for a single request. The portals' `10min_data.csv` is 474 MB, an
order of magnitude over the import body limit, so it arrives as appends against one staging
session and is imported by naming that session.

chunk.description:
The next slice of the file, in file order. The first chunk carries the header row, and a
slice ends where the caller chose: the session holds text, so a row split across two
chunks is rejoined by the append.

session_id.description:
The session to append to. Omitted, a session is opened and its id returned; pass that id
on every later chunk and to the import itself.
The session the file is accumulating in. Name it on the next chunk and on the import.

check_id.description:
The seasonal check a `dry_run` of this file returned (`check.check_id`). A spot or tool
file is screened against the site's seasonal distribution; a commit naming the check is
held to exactly the values it screened, and a commit naming none is refused when the
screen finds a value outside the recorded range.

conflict.description: Behaviour on (stream_id, time, replicate_index) collisions. Defaults to `skip`.

csv.description:
Wide CSV text: a `DateTime`, `Date` or `Time` column plus one column per parameter.
Optional when `session_id` references a previously uploaded CSV.

curves.description:
With `tool`: the standard curve each of the tool's curve slots takes, by slot name, for
every row. A CSV column headed with a slot's name overrides it row by row with the curve
id in the cell (a blank cell falls back to this). The run applies the curve, so outputs
are saved corrected and carry no curve id; the replicates it consumed are saved raw
carrying the curve and its instrument, and the database corrects them.

dry_run.description: When true, resolve and report the plan (and overlap diff) without writing anything.

mapping.description:
Optional explicit column → parameter mapping. The value is a parameter name or UUID;
`null` skips the column. Overrides automatic resolution.

measurement_type.description:
measurement_type stamped on every imported reading ('continuous' | 'spot' | 'derived').
Use 'spot' for lab/campaign result sheets. Omit to resolve per row from the stream's
declaration, then the owning sensor's data_frequency.

session_id.description:
Reference to a staged CSV from a prior dry_run. When present without `csv`, the server
retrieves the cached CSV text instead of requiring a re-upload.

site.description:
Target site, by UUID or case-insensitive name. With `site_column`, the site a row whose
cell is empty belongs to.

site_column.description:
The column naming each row's site, for a file covering several sites: the portals'
high-frequency exports are one wide file per resolution with a `Site_ID` column. Each cell
is resolved like `site`, by UUID or case-insensitive name. Omitted, a header named
`site_id` or `site` is taken as one.

tool.description:
Import the file as tool entry (S4a): each row's columns are inputs of this tool, the tool
runs over every row, and the outputs are saved through the grab write path with the same
server-built provenance a typed entry gets (`source: csv_import`). Without it, columns are
catalog parameters and values import as-is.

tz_offset_hours.description:
Timezone offset (hours) of the source timestamps relative to UTC. The server subtracts
this offset to convert to UTC, e.g. `2.0` for CEST (UTC+02:00).

values.description:
Whether the file holds raw instrument output or already-processed values. Defaults to
`corrected`: no calibration is stamped or applied unless the caller declares the rows raw.

oneOf.description:
The seasonal screen over the file's cells. `null` for a continuous file, which the check
does not apply to (its history is spot readings).

curves.description: One entry per curve slot of the tool (tool entry only): where its curve comes from.

derived_job_id.description:
Background reprocessing job recomputing derived parameters + refreshing aggregates over the
imported range. Poll `GET /api/reprocessing_jobs/{id}` for progress. `null` when nothing was
inserted (idempotent re-import) or on `dry_run`.

derived_timestamps.description: Distinct timestamps queued for derived recompute by that job.

duplicates.description: Readings skipped because they already existed (idempotent re-import). 0 for `dry_run`.

error_count.description: Total number of row problems (may exceed `errors.len()` when the list is truncated).

errors.description:
Per-row problems (bad timestamp / non-numeric value): the offending row or cell is skipped
and the rest import, so the operator can fix the source and re-import. Truncated for very
large files (see `error_count`).

mapped_columns.description: Header → resolved catalog parameter name, for columns that will be ingested.

overlap_sample.description: Up to 20 differing overlaps, so the UI can preview what an overwrite would change.

overlaps_differing.description:
Incoming readings whose (stream, time) already exists with a different stored value.
In `overwrite` mode these are the rows that would be (or were) replaced.

overlaps_identical.description: Incoming readings whose (stream, time) already exists with the same stored value.

overwritten.description:
Stored rows whose value this import changed under `conflict = overwrite`; an identical
overlap is not counted. Always 0 in `skip` mode or `dry_run`.

replicate_groups.description:
(parameter, timestamp) groups holding more than one value in a 'spot' file; each is stored
as one replicate set behind a single served point.

row_count.description: Data rows parsed from the CSV.

session_id.description:
Staging session ID. Returned on every request; pass it back on subsequent requests
(re-analyze, import) to avoid re-uploading the CSV.

site_imports.description:
One entry per site a `site_column` file landed on, in the order they were imported. Empty
for a single-site file, whose totals are the scalar fields.

skipped_columns.description: Columns intentionally not ingested: derived outputs (recomputed) or explicitly skipped.

tool_runs_created.description:
`tool_runs` rows minted by a tool-entry import (one per data row that ran). Always 0 for a
plain import.

unmapped_columns.description: Columns that could not be resolved to a parameter.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notes (e.g. a mapped parameter is not assigned to the site).

ImportCurve.description: How a tool-entry import fills one of the tool's curve slots.

column.description: The CSV column supplying a curve id per row, when one is headed with the slot's name.

standard_curve_id.description: The request-level curve every row takes unless its column cell names another.

measurement_type.description:
Per-reading override ('continuous' | 'spot' | 'derived'). None resolves server-side from
the stream default, then the owning sensor's data_frequency.

standard_curve_id.description: Standard curve the source applied to this reading.

audit.description:
Per-instant expectations from the source portal's own precomputed statistics. Each audited
group's mean/sd is recomputed over the values about to be stored and compared; a
disagreeing group is admitted and recorded as a `replicate_audit_holds` row for review
(`pending` when the stream is paired, `deferred` until pairing otherwise). Sync-service
callers only.

collection.description:
The writer declaring these readings collection events: spot replicate groups sharing an
instant form a `samples` row from the first reading, like `/grab_samples`. Sync-service
callers only; without it a group still forms a sample once it carries two replicates.

oneOf.description:
A completeness claim: these readings are the source's complete content for this stream
over `[from, to)`. The server diffs stored content against the payload and converges —
new rows insert, changed values correct in place, rows absent at source are stamped
withdrawn (never deleted). Sync-service callers only; spot streams only. Without it the
request is a bare append, exactly the old semantics.

accepted_window.description:
The window the server accepted, echoed so a connector can detect an API image that
silently ignored the claim (which would downgrade the source to append mode).

changed.description:
Windowed diff: stored keys the source has moved since river-data stored them. Nothing is
written for them (Q84); `proposed` says how many are waiting for a person.

proposed.description: Windowed diff: changed keys recorded as proposals this pass, each awaiting a decision.

retained.description: Windowed diff: stored rows the funnel refused or the backend dropped, left untouched.

skipped.description:
Readings dropped by admission (out-of-window timestamp, non-finite value, unknown
measurement_type, unknown calibration_id). Reported rather than raised so a cursor-driven
caller can advance past them, and counted so the loss is never silent.

skipped_reasons.description:
One entry per kind of rejection with its count, never one per reading, so the response
stays a fixed size however large the batch.

unchanged.description: Windowed diff: stored rows the payload re-sent unchanged.

withdrawn.description: Windowed diff: stored rows absent from the claimed window, stamped withdrawn.

sensor_id.description:
The instrument the status describes, when the source knows it. None leaves the event
attributed to the stream alone.

deduplicated.description:
Events dropped for repeating the stream's latest value: the series keeps its first
value and its transitions.

skipped.description:
Events dropped because their timestamp is outside the admissible window. Counted rather
than raised, for the same reason `/ingest` counts its skipped readings.

InputRef.description:
One value a formula read at the record's instant. A parameter input carries the slot key
(`parameter_id` with the record's site and time) that resolves its own record; a site property
carries the column it was read from.

formula_code.description: The formula's code, so two formulas producing one parameter stay apart.

replicate_index.description:
Set when the formula evaluates per replicate and this is the variable it iterates: the
value at this index fed the output at the same index.

served_as.description:
How the value was read: `replicate` (the row at the index), `mean` (the family's sample
statistic), `reading` (the single row at the instant), `site` (the site row's column).
`missing` when nothing at the instant answers.

entry_function.description: The function the runner would call. Defaults to `tool`.

manifest.description:
A manifest to set the inspection against. Supplying one adds `reconciliation` to the
response; nothing here reads or writes a stored manifest.

oneOf.description: Present only when the request carried a manifest.

tool_run_id.description: The run to reopen, when the route is the tool.

InstrumentGranularity.description: How many instruments a source's channels stand for, declared by the connector.

InstrumentNameConflict.description: The instrument a proposed name collides with, enough of it to choose by.

has_readings.description: True when it already carries readings; attaching adds to them.

source_system.description: Where it came from, so an operator can tell a hand entry from an earlier import.

is_lab_instrument.description:
Kept as the flag has always read: everything that is not a field device. `kind` is what
says which of the three.

kind.description:
What this row is: `device`, `lab`, `source_parameter` or `entry_channel`. Resolved from the
stored column, falling back to the flag for a row predating the backfill.

site_name.description: The paired slot, when the stream has one.

InvalidatedConfigResponse.description: What an invalidation answers with: the project whose cache was dropped.

KeycloakUser.description:
A realm user as this API reports one: the fields the dashboard renders, plus the realm roles
that decide what they may do. The names are Keycloak's own, so a caller reading the directory
and a caller reading this see one shape.

LastUsedCurveResponse.description:
The instrument and standard curve the newest grab at a site and parameter recorded. Every
field but `method` is null when no grab there names either.

structure.description:

suggested.description: `replicates` only: how many rows the form opens with. The count is never a limit.

The feed's own `(source_system, source_key)` is the identity, and pairing mints the instrument

pairing will mint once a person confirms it. Absent on a plan drafted without one.

than a JSON document nothing describes.

A person has looked at this entry and agreed with it. Set explicitly, never inferred from
an edit: an operator who toggles a parameter group to skip and back has decided nothing.
Only [`ReviewState::NeedsChecking`] entries wait on it; a fully matched entry with no
warning is self-validated and needs no tick.

decimal_places.description:
The decimal places the source declared for this stream, written onto the slot on apply
where the slot declares none. An operator's declaration on the slot is never overwritten.

The device serial the source names for this feed, where it names one. Information the plan
displays; never the instrument's identity.

The lab instrument this stream's standard curves belong to. Present when the stream names
an instrument already, or when its replicate spec names a curve column, and absent
otherwise. A curve is fitted on one instrument, so a reading naming a curve must name that
instrument too; a stream that will carry curve references and resolves to no instrument has
its readings refused (`/readings/batch`) or dropped (`/ingest`), which is what makes this a
decision the plan has to settle rather than report.

is_device.description:
Whether the source reports this feed as a device. That, not the presence of a serial, is
what makes a feed field-shaped: its instrument is minted from the feed's own provenance
when the stream is paired, so the plan proposes no lab instrument for it. A source may
describe a device and report no serial for it, which is why the two are separate.

Present when the stream is a replicate family: what is being paired is the group of
member columns, not the portal's average.

sd_holds.description: Open replicate-statistics holds on this stream, written at plan creation.

Record that a person looked at this entry and agreed with it, or take that back. Separate
from `action`, so changing what an entry does is not the same as deciding it.

clears the source's own description.

Rename the parameter group the source's registry proposes for this column. The code is
re-slugged from the new label, so a rename onto an existing group's label joins that group
instead of creating one. Applied to every entry the same category placed, since a category
is one decision behind every column it holds.

Detach the instrument from every entry this one groups with. Attaching is `instrument_id`;
this is its inverse, since an absent `instrument_id` means "unchanged", not "none".

instrument_confirmed.description: Agree to creating the proposed instrument. Apply refuses while any remain unconfirmed.

instrument_id.description:
Point this entry's curve references at an existing lab instrument instead of the resolved
one. Applies to every entry sharing the same curve column, since one column is one
instrument across the source.

instrument_name.description: Rename an instrument the plan will create. Ignored once it resolves to an existing one.

Which catalog parameter this column is, decided rather than matched: `{"choice":"existing",
"id":...}` attaches to that row, `{"choice":"new"}` creates one under the entry's code. A
`parameter_name` sent without it records `new`, so typing a code that happens to exist does
not attach to it (Q221).

Human display label for the parameter. Takes effect only when apply creates the
parameter (`create: true`); a matched existing parameter keeps its own name.

The coordinates and elevation the apply will create this site with. A site is created once,
so a value the source recorded wrong (an elevation of 1 m) is corrected here rather than on
the site afterwards. Ignored where the entry resolves to a site that already exists: that

twenty-three feeds at one station do not disagree about where it is.

PlanGroupRef.description:
The parameter group a column belongs to, as the source's own registry places it.

A group is one decision behind every column of its category, so the plan carries it on each
entry and the apply creates it once. `ordinal` is the member's position within the group, which
is the registry's own order.

code.description: The group's stable code, slugged from the label the source gives it.

ordinal.description: The member's position within the group.

PlanHeldCurve.description: A source's curve held until this plan attaches it to one of its instruments (Q195).

oneOf.description: Where the apply will create it, or null while nothing is attached, which blocks the apply.

label.description: The source's own label, the curve's parameter cell. It names no instrument.

skipped.description:
The review left this curve behind: it is not stored and the readings naming it are dropped
at the source. A skipped curve does not block the apply.

PlanHeldCurveTarget.description: The instrument a held curve is attached to.

create.description: True when the instrument is one this plan creates.

instrument_id.description: An instrument that already exists. Naming neither clears the attachment.

instrument_source_key.description: The `source_key` of an instrument the plan proposes creating.

skip.description:
Leave the curve behind instead of attaching it: it is never stored and the source stops
sending the readings that name it. `Some(false)` takes the skip back (Q220).

PlanInstrumentGroup.description:
One instrument decision in a pairing plan: the instrument, what it covers, and the curves it
owns. Only instruments the plan actually binds are listed; the rest of the inventory is
reachable through the picker, so this stays a list of decisions rather than a catalog.

anchor_stream_id.description: A stream to address an update to; every entry in the same scope moves with it.

label_candidates.description:
The instruments the curve label matched when it matched more than one. The row is then a
choice between them rather than a suggestion.

name_conflict.description:
An instrument already carrying the proposed name, when the proposal collides with one.
The row is then a choice (attach, or create a second) rather than a suggestion.

proposed_name.description:
What this decision proposed creating, kept through an attach so the picker can offer it
back. Absent for an instrument that was never a proposal.

resolved_by.description:
`stream` | `curve_label` (suggested from the label) | `manual` | `ambiguous_label` (the
label matched more than one, so nothing is suggested) | `placeholder`.

scope.description:
The decision's scope: `column:<curve column>` or `parameter:<source parameter>`, matching
what an update to any member stream settles. Absent for an unbound instrument.

stamps_readings.description: Whether readings under this decision will store a `standard_curve_id`.

PlanInstrumentProposal.description:
Create the lab instruments a plan's confirmed entries ask for, one per `source_key` however
many streams share it, and return them by that key. Find-or-create, so re-running an apply
after a partial failure resolves the same rows.
One row of a source's own instrument register, as the plan puts it to the operator.

The register is the only record of which probe carried which serial and when it was installed,
and it goes with the portal, so it travels ahead of the plan and waits (M185). Admitting one is
the plan's act, like creating a site: nothing exists until the apply runs.

admit.description:
Whether the apply creates it. Proposed admitted: the register is the lab's own record, so
the question is which rows to leave behind rather than which to take. A row that collides
with an instrument already in the inventory is proposed unadmitted instead, because taking
it would leave two rows for one probe (Q76).

attach_to.description: The instrument the review chose to merge this register row onto instead of creating one.

oneOf.description:
The instrument this row would duplicate, by name or by serial. The review answers it the
way the parameter path answers a `name_conflict`: admit as a second instrument, or attach.

metadata.description:
Whatever the register holds that river-data has no column for: the station it was installed
at, the dates, the state the lab recorded.

source_key.description: The source's own identity for it, e.g. `sensor_inventory:62`.

PlanInstrumentProposals.description: The register rows waiting for this source, as the plan carries them.

PlanInstrumentRef.description: The instrument a plan entry's curve references resolve to, and how that was decided.

confirmed.description: A creation an operator has agreed to. Apply refuses a plan holding an unconfirmed one.

curve_column.description:
The source column naming a curve per reading, e.g. `doc_std_curve_id`. Absent when the
instrument came from the stream and no column names a curve (the chla families, corrected
upstream).

defaulted.description:
The instrument row was minted by stream registration rather than named by the source or an
operator (`sensors.metadata.minted_from_stream`). It is the one a review may want to
replace with the real device.

id.description: The resolved instrument, or None when one has to be created.

label_candidates.description:
The instruments a curve label matched when it matched more than one. Which analyser the
source meant is not in the label, so the tie is named and nothing is suggested (Q195).

name_conflict.description:
An instrument that already carries the proposed name. Creating a second one under it is
allowed, and so is attaching to this one, but neither may happen by default: readings
joining an instrument that already holds data is not something a plan decides on its own.

resolved_by.description:
`stream` (already attributed), `curve_label` (suggested from the source's own curve
labels), `manual` (repointed in the review), `ambiguous_label` (the label matched more than
one, so nothing is suggested), or `placeholder` (nothing matched).

source_key.description:
`(source_system, source_key)` is an instrument's identity, so a later rename cannot break
the mapping.

stamps_readings.description:
True when each reading stores a `standard_curve_id` (the family's own calculation names
the curve, members are raw). False when the curve was applied upstream and only the
instrument is attributed, where stamping would correct the value a second time.

PlanJobQueued.description: A plan action that runs as a tracked job: the row to watch, and the state it starts in.

job_id.description:

second job for one plan.

PlanLabelCandidate.description: One instrument a curve label matched, enough of it to choose by.

PlanParamAttach.description:

under the code the entry carries. One field rather than an id beside a flag, so "attached to
nothing in particular" cannot be written down.

oneOf.description: Attach every entry of this group to the catalog parameter with this id.
Create a parameter under the entry's own code.

What the review decided this parameter is, kept on the plan so it survives a reload. Absent
where nobody has decided and the source's own name is still matched against the catalog as a
proposal; a code somebody typed attaches to nothing on its own (Q221).

groups that already exist. Absent where the source declares no category.

label.description:

the parameter, while `name` becomes its `code`.

name.description: The parameter identity: the source's own column name (matches what the portal DB shows).

attach_to.description:
The instrument to merge this register row onto instead of creating one. Sent in place of
`admit` where the review answered a conflict by attaching.

PlanReplicates.description: Replicate-family summary carried on a plan entry, from the stream's registered spec.

PlanSiteDevice.description:
One logger a site's streams name, counted per site: a site instrumented with two loggers has

PlanSiteMetadata.description: What the source knows about one site, as the review renders it beside the pairing.

source_name.description: The name the source sends, which the apply links to the resolved row.

PlanStatusChanged.description: A plan whose status this request moved, with no job behind it.

groups_to_create.description: Distinct parameter groups the source's registry names that the database does not hold.

instruments_to_create.description:
Distinct lab instruments the apply would create, and how many of those an operator has
not yet agreed to. Apply refuses while the second is non-zero.

needs_checking.description:
The three review states over the entries the plan would pair, so the review can say what
share of the plan waits on a person and what share stands on its own evidence.

PlanUnassignedParameter.description:
The source parameters this plan pairs that no instrument covers, so an operator can attach one
where the portal corrected a value upstream without naming a curve per reading.

name_conflict.description:
An instrument already carrying that name. Accepting the suggestion would create a second
one beside it, so the row asks instead of suggesting.

suggested_name.description:
The name an instrument for this parameter would get, proposed the way a site's or a
parameter's name is. Accepting it is what creates the instrument; nothing is minted from a
suggestion alone.

PlanWarning.description:
Something the review has to decide about, carried as data rather than a sentence so the UI can
offer the resolutions instead of only naming the problem. `message` is the rendered form, kept
so a warning always reads as something even where the structure is not used.

source_units.description: The units this source declares, against `existing.units`.

formulas.description: The set as the editor holds it, steps included. One formula is a set of one.
One series per formula of the set, steps included, in the order the set evaluates.

PreviewEventRequest.description:
The cells an operator has typed at a visit and not saved. A cell the request leaves out is one
nobody touched, and reads from the store.

mean.description:
Recomputed here from the served replicates, which is what `samples` holds for a paired
stream. Shown so the review can see the statistics the pairing will produce before it
produces them.

column.description: The source column this index is pinned to, when the stream declares a replicate spec.

calculations.description: The calculations the touched parameters feed, in the order the chain would run them.

not_previewed.description: Everything the preview does not compute, named rather than left to be assumed.

rows.description: The decision's effect on each row, read back from the write itself.

samples.description: The statistics the samples trigger recomputed for the groups the rows belong to.

PreviewUnstagedRequest.description: A preview at a site and instant no visit stands at yet: the typed cells of a new row.

PreviewedValue.description:
One value the chain would produce at a visit, were the staged cells saved. `value` is absent
where the calculation cleared the slot, which a save records as a withdrawal.

output.description: The manifest key the value came out of.

ProjectRef.description: Brief project reference for embedding in responses

ProposeInstrumentsRequest.description: A source's whole instrument register, offered for a plan to admit.

source_system.description: The sync source the register belongs to, e.g. "metalp".

already_admitted.description: Proposals a plan has already admitted, which are instruments now and are left alone.

stored.description: Rows now held as proposals, whether this call created or refreshed them.

calculation.description: The formula that produced a derived value, the counterpart of a tool run's record.

consumed.description:
What the calculation that made this record actually read, captured at the read (Q215),
each input beside what its source holds now. Empty on a record nothing computed, and on
one computed before the capture existed, whose inputs are therefore unknown.

consumers.description:
Every enabled formula reading this parameter, one hop down the chain, with its output's
value at this instant where one exists.

inputs.description:
The values the formula producing this parameter read at this instant, one hop up the
chain. Each names the key its own record is read by.

duplicate_slot.description: More than one stream serves this (site, parameter) at this instant.

parameter_code.description: What the instant measured, named. The record was serving bare numbers under a bare uuid.

records.description: One record per stream serving the instant.

units.description: The slot's unit when it declares one, the catalog default otherwise.

QueuedJobResponse.description:
What a route that enqueues one job answers with: the row it enqueued, and the state that row is
in when the response is written.

job_id.description:
The row enqueued, or null where an identical job was already queued under the same dedupe
key and this request added none.

ReadingCalibrationRef.description: The calibration a listed reading was corrected with.

source_system.description:
The stream's own naming, and the slot its pairing places it in. Filled from the
pairing on read; a proposal against an unpaired stream carries only the source half.

pruned, so an old decision keeps its record and loses only the link to the run.

new.description: What the decision asserts about those columns.

old.description: The projected columns as they stood before the decision.

provenance_kind.description:

unverified.description: A pending entry: stored and shown here, never published (Q18, Q21).

value_arrived_at.description:
When the value this row currently serves arrived: its latest live value correction's `at`,
else its first arrival.

measurement_type.description:
Per-reading override ('continuous' | 'spot' | 'derived'). Omit to resolve from the
resolved sensor's data_frequency (lab CSV uploads should pass 'spot' explicitly).

standard_curve_id.description:
The standard curve the value was corrected with, for a caller replaying grabs that carried
one. Ordinary batch inserts leave it unset. The reading must be a spot measurement on the
instrument the curve was fitted on, and the server recomputes `calibrated_value` from the
curve, so a submitted one is not what gets stored.

measurement_type.description:
Restrict the write to one cadence ('continuous' | 'spot' | 'derived'). 'continuous' also
covers legacy NULL-typed rows.

replicate_index.description:
One replicate of a grab group, which scopes the write to spot rows: a sonde reading sharing
the grab's snapped timestamp must not be flagged by a replicate key. Omit to act on every
row at that timestamp.

calibration_id.description: The time-windowed base calibration the value was corrected with.

collection_event_id.description:
The collection event (site visit) an attributed spot reading belongs to. Stamped by
`collection_events::attach` after the write; NULL on continuous and derived rows.

created_by.description: Who entered it, on a hand-entered measurement.

derived_version_id.description: The formula version a derived value was computed under, on a derived row.

ingested_at.description:
When the stored value arrived (DB default on insert, re-stamped when an overwrite changes
the value). NULL on rows that predate tracking.

label.description: The operator's name for the measurement.

notes.description: The operator's free text about the measurement.

provenance.description:
The server-built record of what produced this value: the tool run and pinned script version,
its resolved inputs, constants and curves, and the outputs it returned. Written by the grab
write path from the stored `tool_runs` row, never by a client.

provenance_kind.description:
Where this value came from: `tool_run` | `chain` | `csv_import` | `manual` | `batch` |
`sync` | `derived`. Total, held by a DB trigger for a writer that names none,
so an unrecorded origin is a named kind rather than a NULL blob (Q49).

standard_curve_id.description: The hand-picked lab curve applied on top of the base calibration, for grab measurements.

An intern's entry that no manager has verified. Curated surfaces leave it out

RunTrace.description:

the formula behind it and the numbers that formula read.

constants.description: The constant values the run resolved, by name.

curves.description: The curves the run applied, as it stored them.

results.description:

tool.description: The calculation's name, as the run recorded it.

enabled.description: Whether the cadence is switched on, where it has one.

interval_seconds.description: Absent where the kind has no schedule at all, which the page reads as on demand.

exclude_replicate_indexes.description: Replicates to leave out, as a flag would.

hold_id.description:

include_replicate_indexes.description: Flagged replicates to bring back, as an unflag would.

migrate_stored.description:

given_up.description:

migrated.description: Whether the migration of the superseded version's values was enqueued.

version_id.description: The version the save minted, or the one it matched: a save that changes nothing mints none.

ScriptInspection.description:
What the runner reads off a script's parse tree without evaluating it.

Every list is a floor rather than a complete set. A script that assembles names at runtime

that is what `dynamic_outputs` and `dynamic_reads` report: while either `any` is true, the
corresponding list is known to be short by an unknown amount.

entry_args.description: The entry function's formals in declaration order; the runner calls them positionally.

outputs.description: The output keys read off the entry function. A floor: see `dynamic_outputs`.

oneOf.description: Null when the script parses. A syntax error is a normal result, not a failed request.

script_functions_used.description:
The script's own top-level functions the entry function calls, which is what a tool

time.description: The entry instant; its month anchors the ±2-month seasonal window.

check_id.description:
Reference for the save: `/grab_samples` validates its readings against this check's
stored entries when the request names it.

SeasonalClass.description:
Where an entered value sits against the seasonal distribution. Only `normal` carries no
warning; everything else is advisory.

SeasonalClassDescription.description: One classification label and what it means, for the method description.

distribution.description: A capped sample of the pooled values, for the distribution plot.

n.description: Pooled historical values in the seasonal window (unflagged spot replicates, all years).

SeasonalMethod.description:

pooled.description: Which rows are excluded and how replicates enter.

statistics.description: The statistics computed over the pooled values.

value.description: Which stored column is compared, and against what.

window_months.description: Half-width of the seasonal window in months.

Selection.description:

optionally bounded by a time window.

calibration_id.description: The readings a calibration corrected, which is what a retirement decides over.

SelectionKey.description: One reading key inside an explicit selection.

value.description:

different number in each, so a value correction over such a selection is one decision with

curve_count.description:

device's states its site: a titrator has no deployment and the Site column is empty for it

kind.description:

SensorUpsert.description:
One instrument from a source's own register, to introduce into river-data.

For a source whose instruments do not each have a stream: every other instrument is minted as a

metadata.description: Whatever the source knows that river-data has no column for.

SourceWindow.description:
A completeness claim over one stream: the readings sent alongside are the COMPLETE content of
the source for this stream over `[from, to)`, read from `source_rows_read` source rows. The
server diffs stored content against the payload and converges (new / changed / withdrawn);
without a window the request is a bare append, exactly the old semantics.

content_digest.description:
Digest of the canonical payload, stamped by the driver before send. The server persists
it on a cleanly-applied pass and echoes it on the stream list, so the next cycle can skip
re-sending unchanged content. Opaque to the server; never computed server-side.

dropped_times.description:
Instants the backend saw but could not carry (cell decode failures). The server retains
stored rows at these keys rather than withdrawing them.

source_rows_read.description:
Source rows scanned to produce the payload. An empty payload over a window the store holds
readings for is refused server-side, so a decode failure cannot read as a source deletion.

StageEventsRequest.description: A field day: the visits it covers, each at its own site and instant.

StageVisitRow.description: One visit of a field day: a site and the instant it was sampled.

StagedCell.description:

records as a withdrawal, so the calculation reads the visit without it.

replicate_index.description: Position in the family. A single measurement is index 0.

standard_curve_id.description: The standard curve the operator picked for this cell, where the slot takes one.

value.description: The number as typed, uncorrected. `null` empties the cell.

created.description: False when the visit already stood at this instant, so a second tool joins it.

unverified.description:

had, so staging into someone else's verified visit does not reopen it.

fitted_on.description: The date the source fitted the curve, which is how the lab identifies one.

notes.description: Whatever the source records about the fit.

StationCandidate.description:
One station offered to a picker: what the list holds, plus how far it is from the site being
configured where that site has coordinates.

distance_km.description: Great-circle distance from the site, absent where either end has no coordinates.

height_barometer_masl.description: The elevation the barometer sits at, which a station reporting no pressure leaves empty.

height_masl.description: The station's own elevation, which every published station carries.

publishes.description:

measurement_type.description: `continuous` or `spot`: which cadence the rows summarise.

total.description: Total events matching the time range (ignores limit/offset)

StepDependent.description:

whose text reads the step's code.

owns.description: Whether the calculation owns the step, rather than declaring one owned by nobody.

StepDependents.description: Everything that reads one step, which is what its page shows before its expression is edited.

shared.description: True when the step belongs to no calculation, which is what makes it shareable (Q156).

StepReader.description: One formula that reads the step.

provenance names it.

name.description: The name the provenance records the subject under.

withdrawn_count.description: Rows stamped withdrawn by windowed reconciliation (included in `reading_count`).

array of such objects (one per replicate), `lists` an object of number lists keyed by field
name.

channel.description:
The channel the row answers for, which is the notification kind (M163). Absent means
`alarm_opened`, the audience every subscriber had before channels were separable.

at.description: Instant of the swap. Defaults to now(). A ends at T, B starts at T (half-open => no overlap).

parameter_id.description:

the site when omitted.

result.description: What the service reported back, shaped by the command it answers.

full_reassert_enabled.description: Whether the weekly `sync_full_reassert` queues a `trigger_full_sync` for this service.

`SyncServiceOperations` from `sync_events`. The column itself has never been written: a
service has no field to report an error through, so the row cannot carry one.

sync_interval_secs.description:

post.description:
The script is parsed in the runner and its tree walked, so an unparseable or hostile script is
inspected as safely as it is read: a syntax error comes back as `parse_ok: false` with the
line, at status 200, because a script being typed is unparseable most of the time.

**`outputs` is a floor, not a complete list.** Keys assembled at run time (`paste0` with a
replicate letter, as pco2 and nutrients do) do not exist in the source, so they cannot be
detected. `dynamic_outputs.any` is true exactly when that happened, and while it is true a
caller must not treat `outputs` as the whole set, nor a manifest declaring more outputs than
were detected as wrong. `dynamic_reads.any` says the same about `inputs`/`constants`/`curves`.

With a `manifest` in the request the response also carries `reconciliation`: which detected
names the manifest does not declare, and which declared names the script does not read,
qualified by those two completeness flags. It is a comparison only, it generates no manifest.
Requires Administrator.

resulting set and activated, whatever the save touched, so an author's version history reads as
their decisions rather than as their keystrokes (Q186). `migrate_stored` chooses what happens to
the values the superseded version produced (Q170). Requires Administrator, or a token with

post.description:
The manifest that is stored is the one an author sent plus the code of every output that named
only an id, so the stored version carries the half that survives leaving this database. A
version is identified by its whole content, and that content is the stamped manifest, so a
manifest-only or case-only edit is a new version. `created_by` is the authenticated caller.
Requires Administrator.

409.description: Script lint or manifest findings, listed in detail

post.summary:
Append an immutable version. Refused when the lint finds forbidden constructs or a syntax
error, the manifest does not parse, an output names a `parameter_id` or the manifest names a
constant that does not exist, an output's `parameter_id` and `suggested_parameter_code` name
different parameters, two outputs resolve to one parameter, or an identical version already
exists. An output whose `suggested_parameter_code` matches no parameter is stored and reported
in `lint`: an author may declare an analyte before a manager creates it.

get.summary: Full version content (script text, manifest, cases). Requires Administrator.

post.description:
A version has to have been validated by hand, **and its cases are run again here** rather than
read off `validated_at`. The stamp says the cases passed at a time, and what a case runs
against outlives it: the constants table and the standard curves a case resolves are shared,
editable state, so a version validated in March can be wrong by June without anything about
the version changing. Activation is the moment it starts answering
`POST /tools/{name}/calculate`, which is the moment worth spending a case run on. The stamp
still gates the workflow, so an author cannot skip seeing the cases pass; it is not the only
thing standing between a failing version and production.

The price is that activation needs the runner: with the sidecar down there is no rollback, and
no tool is calculating anything either way.

The manifest is re-checked against the catalog and the findings come back in `lint`. Those do
not block: a version whose outputs still resolve serves correctly, and refusing to activate it
would leave the operator with no way to put the repaired version live either. Requires
Administrator.
